S2.name: 2 · The contract, and the picture of it

descriptions.root: The repository: the four modules of the chain in its own order, beside what runs them. Working path: AGENTS.md → module names → each module's package and its `config.py` → code; the contract and the overview are the only prose, and a module is read from its own files.
descriptions.Makefile: Entrypoint of everything — the basket `TICKERS`, the per-asset fan-out into one-off runners, `JOBS` measured from cores and memory, the host port from the ports in use, the four `STORE_*_DIR` of this checkout, and `all`, `data-all`, `features-all` and `ml-all`, where the stage order is written down.
descriptions.docker-compose.yml: One image, three anchors, six services: the store environment every service reads, what every service is — and the stores each one mounts, read-only where it only reads, never the code — and the one command the dashboard and the assets share; three runners run a stage and exit, three residents stay up, all under the one project name `liora`.
descriptions.record.py: Measures a stage from outside: wraps one make target, lists the four stores before and after, and writes the run record — knowing no module.
descriptions.AGENTS.md: The contract of this repository: the values, the architecture shape, the canonical vocabulary and the default choice. Every boundary on this picture was decided here, and it is the first thing read.
descriptions.README.md: The overview of the project: the quickstart, the four stores, the chain in order, the basket and the dashboard — what a reader needs before opening a module.
descriptions.module_data/: The data module's repository: its package, its Dockerfile, its pins, its venv Makefile and its one-page README — ingest: venue downloads, Lean ZIPs, one canonical DuckDB per asset.
descriptions.module_features/: The features module's repository — the bars of the timeframe register, the indicator kernels and the feature catalogue, one parquet per timeframe, and the contract `<TICKER>_catalogue.json` the ML layer reads.
descriptions.module_ml/: The research module's repository — the feature set, triple-barrier labels, purged walk-forward XGBoost, the strategy simulation.
descriptions.module_monitoring/: The monitoring module's repository — presentation of what the runtime modules measured, and the one server that serves it; standard library only.
descriptions.sub_module_dx/: This drawing: the tracked tree of the whole repository, rendered by hand with `make dx-update`; the dashboard serves the page below its web root through a read-only bind mount.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/: Per-asset artifacts — one folder per ticker, the asset's whole namespace: its database and every research file beside it. The raw tree and the run records are untracked, so this view does not hold them.
descriptions.store_status/: The three snapshots — data, features, ML — each module's statement about itself, tracked so a fresh clone opens on real numbers, served under `/store_status/`.

descriptions.root: The same tracked tree, read forward: every file and folder of this repository seated beside the primitive it would run on or live in — this view is that mapping, its primitives drawn as icons with the flows between them, and `AGENTS.md` § Pre-AWS architectural direction is the stance it draws. One host with a durable volume is the home of every store, object storage its copy after the run, the stages the states of one machine, the image the code. Described and drawn, built nowhere.
descriptions.image_registry: Four container images in a registry (Amazon ECR): `liora-1m-pipeline`, carrying the packages — pulled by the task host; here it is built by `make build`, and the image carries the code as it would there.
descriptions.task_host: One Linux container instance (Amazon ECS on Amazon EC2): the one host every asset's runs share, its durable volume beside it. It pulls the image, runs the task definitions the state machine starts — once per stage, once per asset — and keeps the dashboard, the panel and one `asset-<ticker>` running as services, one per service, as the residents are kept running here, reached by port-forward and by no public port. An asset is a namespace, never a host of its own; AWS Fargate would be the same task without the host, and so without the volume.
descriptions.store_volume: A durable block volume mounted by every task and service of the instance (Amazon EBS): the `./store_<content>` mounts read as `<volume>/<content>:/store/<content>`, so every store sits at the path its `STORE_*_DIR` names for the service it is granted to, the whole-file lock holds, and no stage changes. The home of state and of nothing of the code — the images carry that; the three stores on the island beside it are its copy, taken whole after the last stage of a run has exited, never by a stage and never mid-run.
descriptions.docker-compose.yml: Four task definitions — one per image, each parameterised by `--tickers` — registered with the service that runs them on the host beside it, never a new unit per asset — and the residents — `liora-dashboard-1`, `liora-devops-1` and one `liora-asset-<ticker>-1` per ticker — as services kept running, one per service, as they are here; the three runners are the task definitions' local spelling, one resident per ticker written out so the parameter stays visible, and the store mounts each service is given are the volume read forward.
descriptions.log_streams: Log streams keyed by stage and container, and metrics (Amazon CloudWatch): every task's output shipped off the host. Here a stage's output reaches the terminal that ran it, and `record.py` keeps a run's time, exit code and store diff. Absent here — described.
descriptions.data_ingest_task: The data-ingest task: the data image run with a `module_data` command (`RunTask` with the command overridden, on the task host) — DownloadMarketData and PublishStatus for data once for the basket, BuildCanonicalData once per asset with `--tickers` narrowed to it — that fetches the venues' public endpoints, writes the raw tree and the asset's canonical market object on the volume and exits, holding nothing between runs.
descriptions.module_data/: The code of the data-ingest task, in its own repository: the venue downloads, the Lean raw format, ingest into the canonical market object and the data status — inside `liora-module-data`, run in the task beside it.
descriptions.asset_store: Object storage with one prefix per asset and version (Amazon S3): `artifacts/<ticker>/<version>/`, the version the run's execution name — the asset folder copied whole from the volume after the run: the one database file and the parquets and JSONs beside it. The copy, never the home; the strategy host reads it here.
descriptions.raw_store: Raw objects under a venue and symbol prefix (Amazon S3): `raw/<venue>/<symbol>/<day>`, one object per UTC day, each written once — the raw tree copied from the volume after the run, Lean-exact so the strategy host could read it as it is. Here it is `store_raw_1m/`, on disk and untracked, so the development view does not hold it.
descriptions.run_store: Run and status objects in object storage (Amazon S3): `runs/<run_id>/` — the record `record.py` writes on the host, one file per stage — and `status/`, the three snapshots' own prefix, both copied from the volume after the run. The reader on the host reads the files on the volume, not this copy. Here they are `store_run_records/`, on disk and untracked, and `store_status/`, tracked in this repository.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/: The asset folders and their home: one folder per ticker on the volume, the tracked README and parameters two of its files; the store beside it is this folder's copy after the run, never its home.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/BTC/: The `BTC` folder on the volume: `BTC_research_ohlcv.duckdb` as the one embedded database — the two venue tables, the canonical table and its three aggregations under one whole-file lock, one writer at a time — copied whole to `artifacts/BTC/<version>/` after the run with the parquets and JSONs keyed `BTC_<artifact>` beside it; never a database process.
descriptions.store_status/: The three snapshots' home on the volume: `STORE_STATUS_DIR`, mounted as `/store/status` and served under `/store_status/` — the `status/` prefix of the run store beside it, read forward; tracked so a fresh clone opens on real numbers.
descriptions.store_status/data_status.json: A status object produced by data compute and read by the page — one row per asset, each carrying its `ticker`; the copy after the run lands under `status/`, the prefix `STORE_STATUS_DIR` already spells.
descriptions.store_status/features_status.json: A status object produced by feature compute — the catalogue's facts and each asset's row counts — read by the page; the same prefix.
descriptions.store_status/ml_status.json: A status object produced by ML compute, a fold over completed asset artifacts, read by the page; the same prefix.
descriptions.ml_research_task: The ml-research task: the features image, then the ml image, each run with its module's command and `--tickers` narrowed to one asset (`RunTask` on the same host), one run per stage from AggregateBars to EvaluateStrategy inside a Map over the basket as wide as `JOBS`, and PublishStatus for features and for ML once each for the basket, never per asset — reading and writing the asset's folder on the volume, and holding nothing between runs.
descriptions.module_features/: The code of the ml-research task's first states, in its own repository: the bars of the register, the feature catalogue and the contract `<TICKER>_catalogue.json` — inside `liora-module-features`, run in the task beside it, one asset at a time.
descriptions.module_ml/: The code of the ml-research task from GenerateLabels on, in its own repository: the feature set, labels, search, model, strategy evaluation and the ML status — inside `liora-module-ml`, run in the task beside it, one asset at a time.
descriptions.dashboard_front: A static front (Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront): the page files and the three snapshots served with no process rendering them — only when a reader outside the host appears; until then the reader container beside it serves them from the volume. Absent here — described.
descriptions.reader_container: The `dashboard` service — `liora-dashboard-1`, the monitoring image — kept running on the task host: the `/containers`, `/runs`, `/store_status/` and `/devops/*` routes of `serve.py`, reading the run records and the snapshots on the volume and reaching the asset services and the panel by name as here; reached from outside by port-forward, where `ssh -L` stands today, and by no public port.
descriptions.module_monitoring/: The monitoring module's repository: the page files — the page and its scripts — inside `liora-module-monitoring`, served by the reader container from the image, the three snapshots read from the status store, the static front absent; `serve.py`'s routes are that container's code.
descriptions.record.py: The record of one run, kept beside the machine's local spelling: it wraps one make target on the host, lists the four stores before and after, and writes `<run_id>/<stage>.json` into the run store — the execution history a state machine keeps for itself, and nothing a task carries.
descriptions.sub_module_dx/: The repository's view — this drawing, a static object served below the page through a read-only bind mount, and not project code; it answers to no primitive of its own, and sits with the documents that deploy nowhere.
descriptions.strategy_host: A separate Linux instance running QuantConnect Lean (Amazon EC2): one strategy container — a lean-backtest task, or one that stays running and trades live — reading the raw objects in Lean's own format and the research artifacts under the asset prefix, its brokerage credentials read once from the secrets store when it starts. No Lean runtime, container or dependency exists here. Absent here — described.
descriptions.brokerage_secret: A secret in a secrets store (AWS Secrets Manager): the brokerage credentials the strategy host reads when it starts to trade live. Locally there is none — the venue downloads use public endpoints, and neither the dashboard nor the panel asks for a credential. Absent here — described.
descriptions.state_machine: A state machine whose states are the stages (AWS Step Functions): DownloadMarketData → BuildCanonicalData → PublishStatus for data → AggregateBars → GenerateFeatures → PublishStatus for features → GenerateLabels → SearchHyperparameters → TrainModel → EvaluateStrategy → PublishStatus for ML, then PublishStores — the copy of every store to its prefix after the last stage has exited. Every per-asset state is a Map over `TICKERS` — 1 wide for BuildCanonicalData, `JOBS` wide above it; the execution name is `run_id`. It starts each task on the host and sits above every stage and inside none — which is why its flows rise over the picture; the Makefile's `all:`, `data-all:`, `features-all:` and `ml-all:` are the same order, read locally.
descriptions.event_rule: A schedule and a condition state (Amazon EventBridge Scheduler; a Step Functions choice): the schedule starts the machine once per `download_cadence_minutes`, a fixed offset after midnight UTC so that the day the download asks for is already full — `is_full_utc_day()` in `module_data/lean.py`; the condition asks the volume whether this asset needs its artifacts rebuilt, and gates the states from AggregateBars on. Today the cadence is a hand typing `make all`, and the condition is the downloaders' own day-presence skip, with the decision to rerun a stage taken by a human at the Makefile. Absent here — described.
descriptions.Makefile: The local spelling of the state machine beside it: `all:`, `data-all:`, `features-all:` and `ml-all:` list the state order, `xargs -P $(JOBS)` is the Map's width, `RUN_ID` the execution name, the fan-out runs one asset's stage in a one-off runner of its module's image, and nothing here schedules — the developer interface, never a scheduler.
descriptions.AGENTS.md: The contract of this repository, where every boundary on this picture was decided — § Pre-AWS architectural direction is the stance this view draws; it deploys nowhere and governs everything that does.
descriptions.README.md: The overview of the project: the quickstart, the stores, the chain and the dashboard; it deploys nowhere and is the first page a reader opens.
